# restate_service_configuration (Resource)

Overrides for the mutable subset of a discovered service's configuration.

### This resource manages settings, not the service

A service is created and destroyed by deployment discovery. This resource neither creates nor deletes one: it applies configuration to a service that already exists, so it must depend on the `restate_deployment` that exposes it.

### Removing it does not revert anything

The Admin API has no operation that resets a setting to the value discovery gave it, and the pinned contract does not define what a JSON null means for these fields. The provider therefore sends only the attributes you set, and never a null.

The consequence is explicit: **`terraform destroy`, or removing an attribute from this resource, stops Terraform managing that setting and leaves the applied value in place.** Nothing is reverted. To restore a discovered default, re-register the deployment with `overwrite = true`, or set the value you want here explicitly.

### Discovery can overwrite these settings

Re-registering the deployment with `overwrite = true` replaces the recorded schema information, which can reset these settings to what the SDK reports. The next `terraform plan` will then show a diff and re-apply them; that is expected, not a bug.

Durations may be written in either the friendly form (`1 day`, `90 minutes`, `30s`) or ISO-8601 (`P1D`, `PT1H30M`). The provider compares them by meaning, so the server echoing a value back in the other form is not a diff.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# This resource manages settings on a service that discovery created; it neither creates nor deletes
# the service. Depend on the deployment that exposes it.
#
# Removing this resource, or removing an attribute from it, stops Terraform managing that setting and
# LEAVES THE APPLIED VALUE IN PLACE. The Admin API has no operation that resets a setting to its
# discovered value, so nothing is reverted. To restore SDK defaults, re-register the deployment with
# `overwrite = true`.

resource "restate_service_configuration" "order_service" {
  service_name = "OrderService"

  # Only reachable from other services, not from the environment's ingress.
  public = false

  # Durations may be written in the friendly form or as ISO-8601; the provider compares them by
  # meaning, so the server echoing one back in the other form is not a diff.
  journal_retention     = "7 days"
  idempotency_retention = "1 day"
  inactivity_timeout    = "1 minute"
  abort_timeout         = "1 minute"

  depends_on = [restate_deployment.orders]
}

# workflow_completion_retention applies only to a workflow service. The provider checks the service's
# actual type and errors rather than sending a setting the service cannot have.
resource "restate_service_configuration" "onboarding_workflow" {
  service_name = "OnboardingWorkflow"

  workflow_completion_retention = "P30D"
  journal_retention             = "P7D"

  depends_on = [restate_deployment.orders]
}

resource "restate_deployment" "orders" {
  http = {
    uri = "https://orders.internal.example.com:9080"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `service_name` (String) Name of the discovered service to configure. Changing it means configuring a different service, so it replaces this resource -- which, per the note above, leaves the old service's applied settings in place.

### Optional

- `abort_timeout` (String) How long Restate waits after `inactivity_timeout` expires, and the invocation has been asked to terminate gracefully, before aborting it.
- `idempotency_retention` (String) How long the result of a completed idempotent invocation is retained.
- `inactivity_timeout` (String) How long Restate waits on a stalled invocation before asking it to suspend. Paired with `abort_timeout`, which starts once this expires.
- `journal_retention` (String) How long an invocation's journal is retained after it completes. Longer retention costs storage but makes an invocation introspectable for longer.
- `public` (Boolean) Whether the service is reachable through the environment's ingress. Set it to `false` to make a service invocable only from other services.
- `workflow_completion_retention` (String) How long a completed workflow's result is retained.

Valid only for a `Workflow` service. The provider checks the service's actual type and reports an error rather than sending a setting the service cannot have.

### Read-Only

- `deployment_id` (String) Deployment currently serving this service.
- `id` (String) Same as `service_name`: a service's name is its identity in the Admin API.
- `revision` (Number) Current service revision. It changes when discovery finds a new schema, which is a useful signal that these settings may have been overwritten.
- `service_type` (String) The service's kind, from discovery: `Service`, `VirtualObject`, or `Workflow`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Imported by service name.
#
# An import adopts every current setting, including values that came from SDK discovery rather than
# from anyone's Terraform configuration. Set only the attributes you actually want to manage; any you
# leave out are not managed and not reverted, and the first plan will show them being dropped from
# state, which changes nothing on the server.
terraform import restate_service_configuration.order_service OrderService
```
